title: Flip building footprints to databridge once a shifted footprints table works
description:
Flip API_SOURCES.liBuildingFootprints from 'arcgis' to 'databridge' once a properly-shifted footprints table works through databridge-api. The databridge branch is BUILT and dormant (LiStore.fillLiBuildingFootprints; LI.vue's area line already prefers square_ft).

## Why dormant

- `li_building_footprints` through databridge works (columns verified incl. square_ft; bin IN / parcel_id_num where clauses translate directly) but its geometry carries the systematic ~0.9m offset vs the Esri basemap (no NAD83->WGS84 shift in the postgres pipelines - see bead vue3-atlas-dzk). Footprints draw at parcel zoom where 0.9m is visible - same reason parcels use the _3857 tables.
- `building_footprints_3857` EXISTS in databridge and has the identical column set (incl. bin varchar, square_ft) but **500s on every query** - even select count(*) - while information_schema lists it fine (verified 2026-09-04). Half-built or missing grants. ASK ROLAND to fix it, or to bless/create an li_building_footprints_3857.
- Note building_footprints (546,374 rows) vs li_building_footprints (546,480) differ by ~100 rows - confirm the _3857 variant is fed from the right source before flipping.

## When flipping

1. Point the SQL in LiStore.fillLiBuildingFootprints at the working shifted table (currently li_building_footprints).
2. Verify at 5036 HAWTHORNE ST: two buildings, bins 1294574 (2056 sq ft, hgt 21) and 1320913 (961 sq ft, hgt 12); footprint polygons should sit ON the basemap buildings, not ~1m southwest... er, offset.
3. square_ft is the TRUE area (matches ST_Area in 2272 exactly); AGO's displayed Shape__Area*6.3225 is a web-mercator approximation ~0.3% high. Numbers will change slightly and be more correct.
4. Related pre-existing bug: bead vue3-atlas-8g6 (unreachable/broken parcel_id fallback + the .data.features misread in other LiStore actions) - both source branches share it; fixing it is separate work.
close_reason: Flipped: building_footprints_3857 works now (Roland's loads), Hawthorne bins verified present and aligned (0.13m/0.12m vs AGO), hand-tested in the L&I topic

title: Replace phila-ui-3 dropdowns/search in Nearby Activity (then City311, CityServices) with compact house controls
description:
Replace the big blocky phila-ui-3 controls (dropdowns + search box) with compact house controls matching the pagination-row search aesthetic.

## Why
The phila-ui-3 packages (@phila/phila-ui-dropdown 0.0.1, @phila/phila-ui-textbox 0.0.2 via TextFilter) are from the abandoned phila-ui 3 line (no dropdown/textbox packages exist in phila-ui-4 - its equivalents are select-field/text-field). Andy has never liked how big and blocky they are. The new compact search-in-pagination-row look (PaginationWithSearch, Sept 2026) is the house style now.

## Where the old controls live (all of them)
- `src/components/topics/nearbyActivity/NearbyActivity.vue` - 2 dropdowns (Activity Type, Time Interval) + TextFilter. THE PILOT.
- `src/components/topics/cityAtlas/City311.vue` - 1 dropdown + TextFilter
- `src/components/topics/cityServices/CityServices.vue` - 1 dropdown
- Registered globally in `src/main.js` (Dropdown, Textbox). Once all three topics are swapped, drop @phila/phila-ui-dropdown and @phila/phila-ui-textbox from package.json and main.js.

## Plan (agreed 2026-09-10)
1. Extract the search input (input + fa-times clear button + pagination-search-* styles) out of `src/components/pagination/PaginationWithSearch.vue` into its own small component. PaginationWithSearch keeps wrapping it, so permits/licenses/condos/docs tables are unchanged. NearbyActivity uses it directly in place of TextFilter.
2. New small house select component: plain native select, 14px, thin #ccc border like the search input, natural width, label inline beside it ("Activity Type: [311 Requests v]") instead of stacked bold on top. Label style is the one open design question - judge by looking.
3. One row on desktop, wrap on mobile. Zone drops from ~230px tall to 1-2 slim lines.

## Key facts making this easy
- The zone only feeds three plain refs down as props: selectedDataType, timeIntervalSelected, textSearch. The seven nearby child tables filter client-side and none paginate. Swap is purely visual - no data logic changes.
- Dropdown API in use: v-model, label, :options (object of value->label). The Time Interval dropdown is v-if'd away for vacant/unsafe types; its options object changes per activity type.
- selectedDataType watcher drives the router (setDataTypeInRouter) - keep the v-model contract identical.

title: Remote tables double-fetch server page 0 on load - dedupe in-flight page fetches
description: fetchPermitsServerPage guards with if (this.liPermitsPages[pageIndex]) return, but the cache entry is only set AFTER the await - so the store's initial fetch (fillLiPermits remote branch) and the component's immediate load() (useRemoteTableUi immediate watch -> permitsUiPage -> fetchPermitsServerPage(0)) both pass the guard and fire identical offset-0 queries (seen in DevTools at 2001 BEACH ST /li). title: Unreachable/broken li_parcel_id fallback in fillLiBuildingFootprints (empty AIS bin)
description:
In `src/stores/LiStore.js`, `fillLiBuildingFootprints()` has a fallback that queries LI_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS by `parcel_id_num` (from AIS `li_parcel_id`) when the AIS record has no `bin` — but the fallback is unreachable, and broken if it were reached.

**Bug 1 — unreachable fallback:** `const feature = GeocodeStore.aisData.features[0].properties.bin.split('|')` — when AIS returns an empty-string bin, `"".split('|')` yields `[""]`, whose `.length` is 1 (truthy), so `if (feature.length)` always takes the bin branch and queries `bin IN ('')` (0 features). The `else` branch can never run. Fix: check the bin string is truthy BEFORE splitting, e.g. `const binString = GeocodeStore.aisData.features[0].properties.bin; if (binString) { ...split and build bin IN (...)... } else { ...parcel fallback... }`.

**Bug 2 — broken fallback body:** the else branch reads `feature.properties.li_parcel_id`, but `feature` is the split array at that point, not the AIS feature — it would throw TypeError. It should read the AIS feature's properties (`GeocodeStore.aisData.features[0].properties.li_parcel_id`).

`_fillLiBuildingCertSummaryArcGIS()` (same file, ~line 179) has the same `bin.split('|')` pattern and inherits the same empty-bin behavior — check it while fixing.

**Repro / discovered via:** 1603 ELLSWORTH ST (atlas .../1603%20ELLSWORTH%20ST/li) shows no buildings in the L&I topic. AIS returns bin="" for that address (base and both condo units; li_parcel_id=42988). NOTE: fixing these bugs will NOT fix 1603 Ellsworth itself — no footprint row carries parcel_id_num 42988; the building over 1603's parcel (bin 1476115) straddles the lot line (58% on 1601's parcel 227331 / 42% on 1603's parcel 42988) and is assigned/addressed to 1601, so AIS has no bin to give. That is an upstream LI_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS data problem to report to CityGeo/L&I. The code fix matters for addresses where the parcel fallback CAN find footprints, and to stop issuing a pointless `bin IN ('')` query.

title: 311 topic stays on secured AGO layer - decided, do not migrate to public_cases_fc
description:
DECIDED 2026-09-03 (Andy + Claude): the cityatlas 311 topic stays on the secured AGO layer `SALESFORCE_CASES_1YEAR`. Do NOT migrate it to Carto `public_cases_fc` or public AGO `PUBLIC_CASES_FC`. Recording so the AGO->Carto audit's "UNCLEAR" verdict on this call site never gets re-investigated.

## Why not

The secured layer carries fields the public 311 feed deliberately omits (verified 2026-09-03 by fetching an AGO token via the app's own generateToken flow and diffing layer metadata against `select * from public_cases_fc limit 1`):

- `DESCRIPTION` / `DESCRIPTION_FULL` — free-text case descriptions (stripped from public feeds for PII)
- `PRIVATE_CASE` — flag; the secured layer includes private cases the public table excludes entirely
- `TYPE_`

And the topic USES the difference: `src/components/topics/cityAtlas/City311.vue` L100 renders `properties.DESCRIPTION` as a table column. A public-table migration would blank it and silently drop private cases from what city staff see.

## How the current auth flow works (so nobody calls it broken again)

- The 311 topic is cityatlas-only (`case 'city311'` in `src/router/index.js` ~L265).
- The router sets `City311Store.agoToken = await getAgoToken()` (router/index.js ~L267-268) before `fillCity311` — easy to miss when reading the store alone; the store's `agoToken: null` initialization is NOT dead state.
- `getAgoToken()` (`src/util/call-api.js` ~L24) posts VITE_AGO_USERNAME/VITE_AGO_PASSWORD (build env / .env.local) to www.arcgis.com generateToken.
- Anonymous queries to the layer return Esri error 499 "Token Required" (service root) / 400 "Invalid URL" (query endpoint).

## If AGO reliability ever threatens this topic

That's a conversation with the 311/Salesforce feed owners about an alternative secured serving path (e.g. databridge with auth) — not a client-side source swap.

Related: AGO->Carto migration branch wip/ago-to-carto; two-source rule in .claude/CLAUDE.md; sibling decision bead vue3-atlas-f9b (ppr_location_types).
close_reason: Decision recorded: won't migrate; secured layer has DESCRIPTION/PRIVATE_CASE fields the public table lacks and City311.vue renders DESCRIPTION

title: Nearby vacant/construction/demolition tables: group repeated rows and link addresses into the L&I topic
description:
Two display changes for three Nearby Activity tables: vacant properties, construction permits, demolition permits (Andy, 2026-09-10).

## 1. Group rows that share common info
A multi-unit project pulls a permit per unit per trade, so the tables show near-identical rows over and over (836 N 4TH ST: 18 distinct permits render as ~18 same-looking rows). Group rows whose displayed columns match (e.g. same address + date + type) into one row - likely with a count so nothing is hidden ("New Construction x4"). Decide whether grouping happens in the SQL (group by + count) or client-side in the component computed; client-side keeps the raw rows available for the map dots.

## 2. Address links into the app
Make each row's address a link that navigates IN-APP (vue-router, not a page load) to that address with the L&I topic open. Route pattern to copy: NearbyActivity.vue's setDataTypeInRouter uses router.push({ name: 'address-topic-and-data', params: { address, topic, data } }) - the L&I topic link wants name 'address-topic' (or the equivalent) with params { address: row.address, topic: 'licenses-and-inspections' } - CHECK the actual topic route param spelling in router config before building.

## Files
- src/components/topics/nearbyActivity/NearbyVacantIndicatorPoints.vue
- src/components/topics/nearbyActivity/NearbyConstructionPermits.vue
- src/components/topics/nearbyActivity/NearbyDemolitionPermits.vue
- (vgt column defs live in each component; address column currently plain text; construction/demolition Type column is plain text, vacant has its own layout)

## Related
- vue3-atlas-z0n proposed adding permitnumber as a column to distinguish the same-looking rows - grouping is the alternative answer to the same problem. Reconcile: if grouping lands, z0n is probably superseded (or permitnumber becomes part of an expanded/detail view).
- Rows come pre-decorated in NearbyActivityStore (distance_ft, link fields); grouping must not break the map-dot geojson computeds which map over the FILTERED rows (they use item.lng/item.lat per row).

title: Report ~0.9m carto-vs-AGO parcel geometry offset to CityGeo; parcels blocked on arcgis until reconciled
description:
Report to CityGeo: carto's parcel tables (dor_parcel, pwd_parcels) disagree with the AGO layers (DOR_Parcel, PWD_PARCELS) by a uniform ~0.9m offset. Ask which pipeline is authoritative and get the other fixed. Until then, atlas's parcel queries stay on arcgis (see API_SOURCES comment in src/config/apiSources.js).

## The measurement (2026-09-03, reproducible)

Comparing the SAME parcel from both sources, WGS84/4326 output both sides:

- dor_parcel mapreg='089N040106' (9 vertices): every carto vertex sits 0.16m EAST and 0.89m SOUTH of its AGO counterpart (max deviation between per-vertex offsets ~0.1m — a rigid shift, not distortion).
- pwd_parcels parcelid='79436' (12 vertices): identical vector, 0.16m E / 0.89m S.
- Same vertex counts, same shapes, same row counts (multi-record mapregs match), same objectid values — same source data, differently georeferenced.

Repro: AGO `.../DOR_Parcel/FeatureServer/0/query?where=mapreg='089N040106'&outSR=4326&f=geojson` vs carto `select the_geom from dor_parcel where mapreg='089N040106'` with format=GeoJSON; diff coordinates.

## Candidate causes (signature fits several; the pipeline configs decide)

- NAD83→WGS84 datum transformation applied in one path and not the other (source data is EPSG:2272, NAD83-based; the shift magnitude matches this region's datum difference)
- US survey foot vs international foot mix-up in the State Plane conversion (2ppm on 2272's large false origin ≈ sub-meter systematic shift)
- Esri applying a transformation the carto path doesn't (or vice versa — we did NOT establish which side is "wrong", only that they disagree; AGO agrees with the DOR basemap tiles, but those are also Esri-served, so that's not independent confirmation)

Note: carto's PostGIS treats ST_Transform 4269→4326 as identity (verified: coordinates unchanged to the last decimal), so no client-side SQL fix exists there.

## Why it matters

- Blocks atlas's parcels migration off AGO (carto branches are built and switchable in ParcelsStore.js, held back only by this).
- ~1m error on parcel boundaries is visibly wrong at parcel zoom against the DOR basemap, in the topic whose text promises boundary fidelity.
- The same question will apply to databridge-api's geometry (2272-native, server-side ST_Transform to 4326) — verify alignment before any map app consumes databridge geometry.

title: Fix pagination of the table in the condominiums topic
description:
The condominiums topic table has broken pagination. When paging past the initially-loaded data, new data is fetched but pagination resets to page 1 instead of staying on the requested page.

## Root Cause
In `src/components/topics/Condos.vue:43-46`, the `condos` computed returns an empty array while data is loading:

```js
if (CondosStore.loadingCondosData) {
  return [];
}
```

When `getDataForPageChange()` sets `loadingCondosData = true`, the table sees 0 rows, vue-good-table re-renders with no data, and the pagination state resets. When loading finishes and rows reappear, the pagination is already back on page 1.

## Reproduction
1. Search "2401 pennsylvania ave" (790 condos)
2. Either:
   a. Page forward to page 11 (where new API data needs to be fetched), OR
   b. Type a page number like 44 directly into the page input box
3. The correct data loads and displays, but pagination resets to page 1 instead of staying on the requested page

Both paths trigger the same bug — next/prev buttons use `nextPage()`/`previousPage()`, and the page input uses `changePage()`, but all three call `getDataForPageChange()` which sets `loadingCondosData = true`, causing the empty-array flash that resets pagination.

## Relevant Code
- **Table component**: `src/components/topics/Condos.vue` — defines the table, pagination options (10 per page), and the `condos` computed that returns `[]` during loading
- **Custom pagination**: `src/components/pagination/CustomPaginationLabelsCondos.vue` — `getDataForPageChange()` (line 153) sets `loadingCondosData = true` during fetch, triggering the reset. All navigation methods (`changePage`, `nextPage`, `previousPage`) call it.
- **Data store**: `src/stores/CondosStore.js` — `fillCondoData()` fetches from AIS API, stores pages in `condosData.pages`

## Architecture Notes
- API returns ~50 items per page; UI shows 10 per page
- Lazy loading: only fetches API pages as the user navigates forward
- `getDataForPageChange()` calculates which API page is needed and fetches missing intermediate pages

title: Decide ppr_location_types migration: Carto plural labels vs baked-in const
description:
Decide how to migrate the Parks & Rec location-types lookup off ArcGIS Online. Blocked on a wording decision Andy needs to ask about (who owns the display labels?).

## Context

`CityServicesStore.fillAllParksRecLocationTypes()` (src/stores/CityServicesStore.js ~L309, called from App.vue ~L56 at startup) fetches the AGO layer `ppr_location_types_atlas` (19 rows) and keeps only `.properties` (geometry discarded). The rows are joined in JS (~L376) against the Carto-fetched PPR facilities to render each facility's "features" text via `display_location_type`.

Verified 2026-09-03 by row-by-row comparison:
- Carto table `ppr_location_types` (19 rows) exists and its `location_type_name` EXACTLY equals AGO's `classify_location_type` in all 19 rows.
- BUT the column atlas displays — `display_location_type` — exists ONLY in the AGO layer. It is a hand-edited singularized variant (e.g. "Swimming Pool" vs "Swimming Pools", "Sprinkler/Sprayground" vs "Sprinklers and Spraygrounds", "Historical/Cultural Attraction" vs "Historic and Cultural Attractions"). That's what the `_atlas` suffix means: atlas-specific display labels, stored nowhere else.

## Options

A. Migrate to Carto `ppr_location_types` using `location_type_name` — accepts plural labels; visible UI text change in the Parks & Rec facility list.

B. Stop fetching over the network entirely: bake the 19 id -> display_location_type pairs into a small const file (copy current AGO values), delete the network call. No backend dependency at all; if PPR adds a 20th type someone adds a line (the join already handles a missing entry gracefully — the facility just omits that label).

Claude's recommendation was B (19 near-frozen display strings don't need a backend), but the label wording is a UI/content decision — Andy is asking whoever owns the AGO layer / the labels before choosing.

## Question to answer before implementing

Who created/maintains `ppr_location_types_atlas` and its `display_location_type` values, and do they care if atlas either (A) switches to the plural names or (B) freezes the current singular names in code?

Part of the AGO->Carto migration work on branch wip/ago-to-carto (two-source rule in .claude/CLAUDE.md).
close_reason: Dilemma dissolved: the owner published ppr_location_types_atlas (with the hand-made display_location_type labels) to carto AND databridge and retired the AGO layer; atlas migrated to databridge with direct-carto fallback - no wording change, no baked-in const needed

title: Auto-failover: fall through to direct carto/arcgis when a databridge fetch fails
description:
Design and add automatic failover for databridge-backed datasets: when a databridge fetch fails, fall through to the dataset's direct carto/arcgis branch at runtime instead of showing an empty topic. Today recovering from a maps-api-proxy outage means a human notices, flips src/config/apiSources.js, and redeploys — fine at a desk, hours at 2am. Andy's driving concern: the proxy chain (lambda -> API gateway -> databridge-api -> carto v3) is new and is now a correlated failure point for ~20 datasets.

## Current state that makes this feasible

- All databridge fetches go through two helpers in src/util/databridge.js (fetchDatabridgeRows, fetchDatabridgeGeoJSON) which return null on any failure.
- Every dataset's fork keeps its direct carto and/or arcgis branches intact (see the source-branch rules in .claude/CLAUDE.md — never delete a working branch; every dataset keeps a proxy-independent one).
- So the shape is: instead of `if databridge { data = await fetchDatabridge...; if (!data) return; }`, the null case falls through to the next branch.

## Design questions to settle first (don't just bolt it on)

- Loud, not silent: console.warn at minimum when failing over, ideally a store flag the UI could surface — silent failover masks proxy problems and delays anyone noticing the outage.
- Per-call vs sticky: fail over per request, or set a session-wide "databridge is down" latch after N failures so every subsequent call skips the doomed attempt (and its timeout)?
- Timeout tuning: a hung lambda (not a fast 500) means each failover costs the axios timeout — consider a short explicit timeout on the databridge helpers so failover is snappy.
- Which fallback: per-dataset preference order (carto first where it exists, else arcgis)? Could live in apiSources.js as an ordered list instead of a single string.
- Testing: how to exercise the failover path on demand (a debug flag that forces databridge failures?).

Related: the cosmetic cleanup debt (functions named _fillXCarto now serving multiple SQL transports; AGO setup lines hoisted above forks in fillLiBuildingFootprints etc.) could ride along with this work since it touches the same forks.

title: queryDatabridge 503 under cold page load - documented as-is, no proxy changes made
description:
﻿Document of a maps-api-proxy queryDatabridge 503 under real page load, exactly as observed 2026-09-09. NO changes made to maps-api-proxy (deliberately - Andy wants the problem captured as-is first).

## Symptom

Loading localhost atlas L&I topic for 990 SPRING GARDEN ST (~12 simultaneous databridge requests), the business-licenses count query returned **503 Service Unavailable** from API Gateway (`haydr3k097.execute-api...`, Apigw-Requestid DchDNhc1IAMEbuA=, response Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 19:09:20 GMT, Content-Length 33). Client-side cascade then made it worse: count failed -> store fell through to the non-remote fetch-all path -> that hit the databridge 1000-row cap (1,439 licenses) -> Business Licenses displayed (0).

## Evidence gathered (all same afternoon, warm system)

- The EXACT failing count SQL, rebuilt from the store code with the address's real AIS values (li_address_key 545326, eclipse 132721063|15601604, opa 883523100, pwd 513517): **succeeds standalone in ~900ms, n=1439**. The query is not the problem.
- Each WHERE condition individually: 200-1000ms.
- 15 truly-simultaneous light requests (HttpClient async, one process): all 200.
- 12 truly-simultaneous HEAVY queries mirroring the L&I page (licenses count + page, opa, footprints geojson, permits page, case_investigations/violations/appeals selects, regmaps envelope, parcel geojson): **all 200, total wall time 2.1s**. Warm capacity is fine.

## Hypothesis (unverified - needs CloudWatch)

Cold-start pileup against reserved concurrency. queryDatabridge's weight in maps-api-proxy lib/params.ts is 1 -> roughly 5 reserved concurrent executions (200-execution pool / ~37 total weights). A first-load burst of ~12 requests against 5 cold containers -> throttles, which API Gateway surfaces as 503. All my probes ran against a warmed lambda and cannot reproduce the cold case.

Alternative: individual requests exceeding the lambda's 12s timeout under cold-start + contention. Distinguishable from throttling in CloudWatch.

## How to verify (Andy, oit-se-cc console)

CloudWatch -> Lambda metrics for the queryDatabridge function around 19:09 GMT 2026-09-09:
- **Throttles** > 0 at that minute -> concurrency undersizing confirmed
- **Duration** near 12,000ms / errors -> timeout path instead
- ConcurrentExecutions curve shows the burst shape either way

## Candidate fixes (when ready - maps-api-proxy changes, none made)

- Raise the concurrency weight in lib/params.ts (queryAis has 10 for one dataset; queryDatabridge now serves ~20 across atlas)
- Revisit timeout (12s) / memory only after metrics say which lever matters
- Note the lambda is now atlas's whole data plane; sizing decisions made for the single-dataset pilot no longer fit

## Mitigation already in atlas (NOT the fix)

LiStore._fetchLiSql falls back to direct carto with a console.warn when a databridge call fails (scoped instance of bead vue3-atlas-h1v). This keeps topics rendering through proxy hiccups but must not hide the sizing problem - the console.warn is deliberate.


## VERIFIED 2026-09-09 (CloudWatch, oit-se-cc, function MapsApiProxyStack-queryDatabridgeFunctionE89B2468-PeykZFDYFXLq)

- Throttles: max 9 in the testing window (~18:55-19:15 UTC) - CONFIRMED throttling
- Total concurrent executions: pinned at exactly 5 = the reserved-concurrency ceiling (weight 1 in lib/params.ts)
- Duration: avg 419ms, max 3,755ms - nowhere near the 12s timeout; timeout theory ruled out
- Errors: 0 / success 100% - throttled requests never invoke, so the function itself looks healthy

Root cause settled: reserved concurrency of 5 is undersized for atlas page loads that burst ~12 requests. Fix (when chosen): raise the queryDatabridge weight in maps-api-proxy lib/params.ts.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in prod: maps-api-proxy PR #68 (queryDatabridge weight 1->10, reserve 5->40) deployed to prod 2026-09-10; a 12-simultaneous heavy-query burst mirroring the L&I page load returns 12x 200 (previously throttled at the 5-concurrent ceiling). Andy reports no breaking API calls in the app.

title: Dates show one day early wherever timestamps are UTC midnight (rendered in local time)
description: App-wide display quirk, predates the databridge migration and matches prod: date-typed values arrive as UTC midnight ('2026-06-25T00:00:00Z'); vue-good-table date columns (dateInputFormat yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssX, output MM/dd/yyyy) and date() formatters parse to local EDT/EST, landing the previous evening, so 06/25 displays as 06/24. Verified in Nearby Activity construction permits (screenshot vs raw rows, uniform -1 day). Fix idea: format date-only fields in UTC (or slice the yyyy-MM-dd before parsing) - audit ALL vgt date columns and useTransforms date() so the fix is consistent; check against prod so we do not 'fix' a table into disagreeing with the source system's own site (li.phila.gov shows the same permits - compare there).
notes: FULL PICTURE 2026-09-11 (Andy's skepticism drove this): FP-2021-003472 at 2001 BEACH ST - EVERY mirror stores calendar date Nov 4 (carto: 2024-11-04T05:00:00Z = midnight EST; databridge: naive midnight; AGO: epoch = Nov 4 00:00 UTC), while li.phila.gov (which reads AGO per L-I-Consolidation src - NOT Eclipse directly) and atlas-on-databridge both display Nov 3. Stored=displayed+1 uniform across 5 sampled permits. CONFIRMED by Andy in browser: PROD atlas (direct carto, midnight-EST serialization) displays 11/04 - so atlas and li.phila.gov DISAGREE in prod today, and the databridge branch (UTC-midnight serialization -> 11/03) brings them into agreement on release. STILL UNKNOWN: the true Eclipse date - all witnesses share ETL ancestry; either storage is +1 everywhere or displays are -1 everywhere. RESOLVE by asking Roland/L&I to read FP-2021-003472's issue date out of Eclipse itself. DO NOT change display code until that answer is known; any fix must be coordinated with storage, and display behavior depends on which serialization form comes back.
close_reason: Resolved: L&I (Daniel Whaland) confirmed the stored calendar date is the true date (FP-2021-003472 = 11/4); normalizeTimestamps now renders every midnight form as the local calendar date, so atlas displays stored dates verbatim on both transports; li.phila.gov's -1 shift is the actual bug (tracked in vue3-atlas-qtr)

title: L-I-Consolidation: li.phila.gov shows all date-only fields a day early (timezone parse)
description: CONFIRMED WRONG by Daniel Whaland (L&I, Teams 2026-09-11): FP-2021-003472's true issue date is 11/4/2024; li.phila.gov shows 11/3. Mechanism: AGO serves date-only fields as epoch = midnight UTC of the TRUE date; epochToIso (L-I-Consolidation src/store/index.js ~line 9) makes a Z-suffixed ISO string; moment then parses to Eastern local, landing the previous evening, so the formatted date is -1 day. Fix: render date-only fields as the UTC calendar date (moment.utc, or slice the yyyy-MM-dd off the ISO before parsing). Audit EVERY epochToIso'd field: permitissuedate, casecreateddate, mostrecentinvestigation, casecompleteddate, initialissuedate, inactivedate - plus any other date formatting in the app. Verify against the Eclipse-confirmed specimen: FP-2021-003472 at 2001 BEACH ST must show Nov 4. Context: atlas's equivalent handling was fixed 2026-09-11 (normalizeTimestamps in vue3-atlas util/databridge.js renders stored calendar dates verbatim) - see closed bead vue3-atlas-qt1 for the full investigation. Repo has no beads tracker, so this lives in the atlas tracker. Do NOT start mid-atlas-release-work - soon after.
